main_chase_cards.name: Celebi
main_chase_cards.why: Celebi is the hinge of this file: the little time-travel myth that makes Premium File 3 feel like a threshold object before Awakening Legends. The collector interest is not just that Celebi is desirable; it is that this print arrives as part of a deliberately arranged nine-card page where types, legends, and connected art teach the Neo era how to look assembled.

key_artists.name: Sumiyoshi Kizuki
key_artists.why: Kizuki's Celebi matters because the artwork is not isolated; it is one panel of a connected Celebi / Sudowoodo / Sneasel scene. Her soft, storybook handling turns a catalog row into a little forest encounter, which is exactly the kind of assembly a collector agent should preserve.

key_artists.name: Naoyo Kimura
key_artists.why: Kimura's legendary-beast combined artwork belongs to the broader Premium File 3 product context; this catalog UID does not model those rows, but agents should know why complete-file listings often invoke the beasts alongside Celebi.

claims.text: Bulbapedia's Neo TCG Era merchandise page gives Premium File 3 / プレミアムファイル3 a November 23, 2000 release date.
The broader Premium File 3 product is described as a nine-card special-card set and precursor to Awakening Legends, collectively representing every TCG type.
not_claiming: that this local UID models all nine rows

claims.text: The broader Premium File 3 card list includes Celebi, Entei, Suicune, Raikou, Lugia, Sudowoodo, Skarmory, Sneasel, and Ho-Oh.
The local catalog models only the unnumbered Celebi source row for this release family; the broader nine-card product context is preserved as legible context, not as modeled row coverage.

Bulbapedia's combined-illustration reference links Celebi with Sudowoodo and Sneasel in a Sumiyoshi Kizuki connected-art group, while Entei, Suicune, and Raikou form a separate Naoyo Kimura Premium File 3 group.
Bulbapedia identifies Sumiyoshi Kizuki / 木月すみよし as a Pokemon TCG illustrator whose style was often noted for a soft crayon-like look and whose early TCG work began around Team Rocket.

Premium File 3 is not merely a checklist stop: it is a compact Neo-era page-object where Awakening Legends, type coverage, legendary Pokemon, and connected illustrations arrive together before the expansion pack version of the story.
This release dossier carries a special identification packet for the Premium File 3 Celebi source-row boundary.

narrative.human_title: Premium File 3 Celebi — the time traveler in a nine-card Neo page
narrative.why_it_matters: Premium File 3 is where the Neo era starts arranging itself like a little museum page. Celebi is the card our local unnumbered-promo slice can actually model, but the emotional charge comes from the surrounding object: nine special cards, every TCG type represented, legends stacked around a new mythical time traveler, and connected artwork that lets a collector see the file as one composed scene rather than nine loose rectangles. That is the assembly worth preserving.

special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat this local release UID as the Premium File 3 Celebi source-row route, not as proof that all nine Premium File 3 cards are present or modeled under the UID.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, seller note, or agent memory says Celebi, セレビィ, Serebii, Premium File 3, プレミアムファイル3, Awakening Legends, Neo Revelation, Psychic Leaf, Sumiyoshi Kizuki, Sudowoodo, Sneasel, or source index 210.
steps: Anchor the broader product to Premium File 3 / プレミアムファイル3, released November 23, 2000 as a precursor to Awakening Legends.
Remember the product-level frame: nine special cards representing all TCG types, with many Legendary or Mythical Pokemon.
Preserve source index 210 as the local catalog's Celebi route; do not treat this UID as complete coverage of the other eight Premium File 3 cards.
Confirm the candidate row is Celebi / セレビィ / Serebii, No. 251, Grass type, Basic, HP 50, with Psychic Leaf.
Use Sumiyoshi Kizuki / 木月すみよし as the expected Celebi artist credit.
Use the connected-art clue: Celebi belongs with Sudowoodo and Sneasel in a Sumiyoshi Kizuki combined illustration.
Separate product-level Premium File 3 context from card-level seller evidence; a file listing does not prove Celebi is present, original, attached, or undamaged.
Separate this print from Neo Revelation English/Japanese expansion numbering, Awakening Legends booster-pack rows, later Celebi promos, Shining Celebi, movie Celebi, and modern classic reprints.
If a seller claims a complete Premium File 3, ask for full-file photos plus close photos of Celebi, because file completeness and card identity are separate claims.
Before any funded trade, require seller-controlled evidence for the exact physical card or sealed/file object being claimed.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Celebi as source index 210 in the Neo Era Premium File 3 unnumbered-promo source row.

The Celebi page and marketplace metadata converge on the row-level signals: Grass-type Basic Pokemon, HP 50, No. 251, Fire weakness, one retreat cost, and Psychic Leaf.
The Celebi row is illustrated by Sumiyoshi Kizuki / 木月すみよし.

Celebi's collector meaning in this route comes from its position as a Premium File 3 / Awakening Legends bridge and from the way its art connects to surrounding cards, not from name-only scarcity.

narrative.human_title: Celebi — source index 210, the little time traveler in the file
narrative.why_it_matters: This Celebi is easy to flatten into a name and a price, but that misses the card. It is a file-born Celebi, a small mythical Pokemon carried into the TCG through the Neo era's page logic: all types represented, legends orbiting it, Awakening Legends just ahead, and Sumiyoshi Kizuki's soft connected illustration making Celebi feel less like a trophy and more like a quiet visitor in a forest with Sudowoodo and Sneasel nearby.
